status: prototype - not a final production spec, see docs/animation-policy.md

pivot.basis: fixed across all animations/frames of this character; horizontal = shared silhouette center, vertical = lowest observed hover-pod position among the adopted Idle frames (virtual ground line). proto_one is a hover-type character with no literal foot contact. Walking and Sprinting both reuse this exact pivot (not independently re-fit) so switching between animations in-game does not pop the character's position or scale.

Turn.notes: One-shot direction-change transition, not a looping locomotion cycle: frame 00 = facing left, frame 01 = stylized spin/twist motion-blur effect, frame 02 = facing right. No corresponding code MovementState exists yet (see animation-policy.md); this is asset-only preparation ahead of movement-logic wiring.

Jumping.notes: One-shot takeoff sequence (matches code MovementState Jumping, which the doc's animation vocabulary calls Jump Start + Airborne combined), not a repeating cycle - frame 00 = ready/crouch pose, frame 01 = thrust launch with visible downward propulsion trail from all 3 hover pods, frame 02 = airborne pose. fps/loop are independent candidates, not part of the Current Animation Contract.

Falling.notes: Unlike Turn/Jumping, Falling loops: descent duration is variable (depends on fall height/state), not a fixed one-shot burst, so it is treated as a sustained state like Idle/Walking/Sprinting rather than a bounded transition. fps=6 is an unconfirmed independent candidate, not part of the Current Animation Contract.

notes: 2026-09-10: frames/idle raw source PNGs were fully replaced by the user and re-normalized from scratch (previous values backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-oldframes). Schema unchanged; canvas stayed 128x128; pivot.y shifted 124->123 due to the new source's tighter bbox. New source set has visibly less body-scale jitter than the previous one (bbox width varies by only ~3px across all 4 frames vs ~85px before). Same day: Walking animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-walking). Walking=4 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (source had exactly 4 raw frames, within the existing 3-4 candidate range). Walking's normalized frames were scaled independently (0.1329 vs Idle's 0.1429, since Walking's raw union bbox is larger) but deliberately mapped onto the SAME fixed pivot (64,123) as Idle so the two animations share a stable ground line and center when swapped at runtime. 2026-09-10 (later same day): proto_one_walking_01 (from raw walking02.png) measured as a body-silhouette outlier (antenna tip and cyan glow excluded from the measurement) - body bbox 103x102px on the 128 canvas vs 93-97x96px for the other three. Corrected by rescaling that single frame 0.933x around the fixed pivot (64,123) only, with no change to crop/scale of the other three frames and no per-frame re-centering. Post-fix body bbox is 96x95px, within the other frames' range. Previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-walking-rescale. 2026-09-10 (later same day): Sprinting animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-sprinting). Sprinting=4 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (source had exactly 4 raw frames, within the existing 4-6 candidate range for Run). Same body-silhouette-outlier check as Walking was run proactively before normalizing (antenna tip and cyan/white glow-trail pixels excluded via a blue-channel filter, verified against a debug mask overlay) - the largest frame (sprinting02) was only ~2-3% larger than the other three, well under the threshold that triggered Walking's correction, so no per-frame rescale was applied here. All 4 frames share the same crop/scale and the same fixed pivot (64,123) as Idle/Walking; Sprinting's raw union bbox (840x978) is the largest of the three states so far, giving the smallest per-state scale (0.1196) - expected and correct, not an error. fps set to 8 (vs Idle/Walking's 4) as a candidate value to match Sprint's higher-energy read; this fps choice is NOT part of the Current Animation Contract (which only governs frame count) and remains an independent, unconfirmed candidate. 2026-09-10 (later same day): Turn animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-turn). Turn=3 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract as a NEW row (Turn did not previously exist in the contract table) - the raw source had exactly 3 frames, which exceeds the old non-binding candidate range of ~1-2 but the candidate table is explicitly advisory, not binding, so the actual provided asset count was adopted. Turn's 3 raw frames are not simply pose variations of one category: frame 1 and frame 3 are mirrored static facing poses (left vs right), while frame 2 is a categorically different stylized spin/twist motion-blur effect frame. The body-silhouette-outlier check was applied ONLY between frame 1 and frame 3 (the two comparable static poses) - they measured 101x99 vs 111x105 on the 128 canvas (~9% mismatch), so both were corrected toward their shared average via pivot-anchored rescale (frame 1 x1.040, frame 3 x0.963, both anchored at the fixed pivot (64,123)), landing at 106x104 vs 107x101 after correction. Frame 2 (the spin-blur) was deliberately left unmeasured/uncorrected: the row-profiling body-silhouette method is not meaningful for it (most of its pixels are the excluded cyan/white glow trail, not opaque body material), and its larger, more dynamic footprint is treated as an intentional effect (comparable to how Air Dash is expected to use stretch/afterimage per animation-policy.md section 8), not a jitter bug to fix. All 3 frames still share the same crop/scale and the same fixed pivot (64,123) as the other animations. loop is false (unlike Idle/Walking/Sprinting) since Turn is a one-shot transition, not a repeating cycle. 2026-09-10 (later same day): Jumping animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-jumping). Jumping=3 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (raw source had exactly 3 frames; code MovementState Jumping maps to this doc's Jump Start (~1) + Airborne (~1-2) combined, whose candidate ranges sum to ~3, so no conflict). All 3 raw frames are the same pose category (unlike Turn) - no mirrored or effect-only frame here, though frame 2 (jumping02) does carry a bright downward thrust-trail effect on its hover pods. Body-silhouette measurement (same blue-channel glow exclusion, re-verified against a debug mask) showed width very consistent across all 3 (90-94px on the 128 canvas, ~4%) but frame 2's body height measured shorter (86px vs 94px for the other two, ~8.5%). This was deliberately NOT corrected with a pivot-anchored rescale: visual inspection of the contact sheet shows the head/dome - the dominant silhouette element - is the same size in all 3 frames, and the height gap is concentrated in the hover-pod region only, consistent with pods being drawn tucked closer to the body during active thrust versus hanging relaxed at rest. A uniform rescale would incorrectly shrink the already-correct head to chase a pose difference, not a scale error, so no correction was applied - unlike Walking/Turn where the same tool WAS the right fix because the discrepancy there was a uniform whole-body scale inflation. fps=8/loop=false are independent candidates (Jumping is treated as a bounded one-shot takeoff, not a repeating cycle), not part of the Current Animation Contract. 2026-09-10 (later same day): Falling animation added (previous manifest backed up at proto_one.manifest.json.bak-before-falling). Falling=3 frames was adopted in animation-policy.md's Current Animation Contract (raw source had exactly 3 frames; code MovementState Falling maps to this doc's Airborne (~1-2), so the provided count exceeds that non-binding candidate range - documented as such rather than silently ignored). All 3 raw frames are the same pose category, no mirrored or effect-only frame. Body-silhouette measurement showed width tight across all 3 (95-96px on the 128 canvas) but frame 0 (falling01) measured notably shorter (95px height vs 102-104px for the other two, ~8% gap) while frames 1 and 2 already agreed closely with each other (102 vs 104, ~2%). This pattern - one frame off, the other two mutually consistent - matches the Walking-type uniform-scale-error case rather than the Jumping-type intentional-pose-difference case, so frame 0 alone was corrected via pivot-anchored rescale (x1.047 about the fixed pivot (64,123)), landing at 100x98px, in range with the other two. Falling is set to loop=true (unlike Turn/Jumping) since a fall's duration varies with height and isn't a fixed one-shot burst; fps=6 is an unconfirmed independent candidate. Not part of the Current Animation Contract, which governs frame count only.
